subject: Hospitality
title: Menu Descriptions That Sell
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Menu Descriptions That Sell.

hook.text: 'Grilled chicken breast' sells for $15. 'Free-range chicken, herb-marinated and flame-grilled' sells for $22.

buildup.text: Descriptive labels boost sales by 27% per Cornell research. Words like 'slow-roasted' and 'hand-crafted' trigger cravings.

discovery.text: Nostalgic labels work too: 'Grandma's pot roast' or 'old-fashioned lemonade.' They evoke emotion and memories—not just flavor.

twist.text: Over-description backfires. A menu with 50-word item descriptions overwhelms guests.

climax.text: Great menu copy sells the experience, not the recipe. You're not buying chicken—you're buying the story of where it came from.

punchline.text: 27% more sales from better words. Menu writing is the cheapest marketing that exists.

quiz.question: By how much can descriptive menu labels increase sales?
